Sea-ice extent over the latest twenty calendar years, including 2026¶

A focused supplement to the full-record monitoring notebook

The window now includes the latest observed year: 2007–2026, through 10 November 2026 in the present snapshot. 2006 is outside the window. The current year participates in the primary analysis, rather than being confined to an appendix. Every plot, table, fit, and conclusion is regenerated below.

To compare equal seasons, the headline yearly statistic is the matched year-to-date (YTD) mean, January 1 through the latest available month and day in each of the twenty years. February 29 is omitted in every year. Completed 2026 months and seasonal windows enter their corresponding fits; unfinished or unavailable months stay missing. Full-calendar-year means are a separate supporting statistic and do not assign a full-year value to unfinished 2026.

The fixed 1991–2020 climatology remains the named reference, not a fitted trend window. Recent fast-track values are included where available and flagged as provisional, with a nominal-only sensitivity check. Short-record intervals are conditional statistical estimates, not a complete measurement uncertainty budget or evidence of acceleration, a regime shift, or a future trajectory.

Run from the project directory; no network access or raw-data changes are needed. Exports are written to artifacts/sea_ice_last_20_years/ independently of the full-record analysis. The window advances with the year of the latest observation.

1. Definitions and declared analysis choices¶

Extent is the ocean area of grid cells with sea-ice concentration ≥15%, not concentration-weighted ice area, thickness, or volume. Raw text values are in km²; calculations and plots use million km². The product is EUMETSAT OSI SAF Sea-Ice Index v3.0, OSI-420-a. Product User Manual §§6.2.2, 8.3.1.

The same conservative rules as the full-record notebook apply: mask -999, retain provider interpolation flags, add no interpolation, require every day for a monthly or full-calendar-year mean. Matched YTD means require every day in the same Jan 1–cutoff window, excluding February 29. Available provisional values enter the primary YTD and completed-month analyses with explicit flags; a nominal-only comparison uses an earlier shared cutoff in all twenty years. Full-calendar-year means weight days equally, unlike the provider's equal-month yearly index. Daily baselines align by month and day; February 29 has eight actual reference observations. The 1991–2020 reference is fixed throughout.

Slopes are ordinary least squares (OLS). Primary uncertainty is a pointwise 95% approximate Student-t interval from calendar-aware Bartlett/Newey–West HAC covariance, 3 annual lags, small-sample correction n/(n−2), and n−2 degrees of freedom. The shared helper preserves actual calendar lags when an influence check removes a year. With only twenty annual observations these intervals are approximate; diagnostics and sensitivity checks are essential. Newey & West (1987), statsmodels HAC assumptions.

Intervals quantify regression sampling uncertainty conditional on the selected linear model, not the full satellite retrieval, baseline, calibration, mask, or model uncertainty. A confidence interval containing zero does not demonstrate that extent is stable or recovering.

from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import calendar
import hashlib
import importlib.metadata
import json
import platform

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib as mpl
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
from matplotlib.colors import TwoSlopeNorm
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests
from IPython.display import display, Markdown
import nbformat

from sea_ice_monitoring import (
    NAMES, load_series, calendar_climatology, with_anomalies, aggregate_periods,
    seasonal_extrema, linear_trend, trend_record, circular_block_bootstrap, matched_ytd,
)

ROOT = Path.cwd()
OUTPUT = ROOT / 'artifacts' / 'sea_ice_last_20_years'
OUTPUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
BASELINE = (1991, 2020)
WINDOW_YEARS = 20
HAC_LAGS = 3
ALPHA = .05
BOOTSTRAP_DRAWS = 4000
SEED = 20261111
UNITS = 'million km²'
COLORS = {'nh': '#17679A', 'sh': '#C16A27', 'global': '#31745B'}
tables, figure_names = {}, []
RUN_TIME = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
versions = {p: importlib.metadata.version(p) for p in
            ['numpy', 'pandas', 'matplotlib', 'scipy', 'statsmodels', 'nbformat', 'nbclient']}

mpl.rcParams.update({
    'figure.figsize': (11.5, 5), 'figure.dpi': 110, 'savefig.dpi': 300,
    'font.family': 'DejaVu Sans', 'font.size': 10, 'axes.titlesize': 12,
    'axes.titleweight': 'bold', 'axes.spines.top': False, 'axes.spines.right': False,
    'axes.grid': True, 'grid.alpha': .18, 'axes.axisbelow': True,
    'legend.frameon': False, 'pdf.fonttype': 42,
})
pd.set_option('display.max_columns', 18)

def show_table(name, frame, decimals=3):
    tables[name] = frame.copy()
    display(frame.round(decimals))

def save_figure(name, fig, caption):
    fig.text(.01, -.025, caption, fontsize=8, color='#555555', ha='left', va='top')
    for extension in ('png', 'pdf'):
        fig.savefig(OUTPUT / f'{name}.{extension}', bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
    figure_names.append(name)
    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)

def fit_values(result, years):
    return result['intercept_at_center'] + result['slope_decade'] / 10 * (np.asarray(years) - result['center_year'])

def calendar_axis(index):
    return pd.to_datetime('2000-' + pd.DatetimeIndex(index).strftime('%m-%d'))

def in_window(index):
    return (index.year >= START_YEAR) & (index.year <= END_YEAR)

all_frames = load_series(ROOT)
AS_OF = min(f.extent.last_valid_index() for f in all_frames.values())
END_YEAR = AS_OF.year
LAST_COMPLETE_YEAR = END_YEAR if AS_OF == pd.Timestamp(END_YEAR, 12, 31) else END_YEAR - 1
START_YEAR = END_YEAR - WINDOW_YEARS + 1
MID_YEAR = START_YEAR + 10
YEARS = np.arange(START_YEAR, END_YEAR + 1)
frames = {h: f.loc[in_window(f.index) & (f.index <= AS_OF)].copy() for h, f in all_frames.items()}
climatologies = {h: calendar_climatology(f, BASELINE) for h, f in all_frames.items()}
monthly_full = {h: aggregate_periods(f, 'ME') for h, f in all_frames.items()}
annual_full = {h: aggregate_periods(f, 'YE') for h, f in all_frames.items()}
monthly, annual, monthly_normals, annual_normals = {}, {}, {}, {}
daily = {h: with_anomalies(f, climatologies[h]) for h, f in frames.items()}
for h in frames:
    ref_m = monthly_full[h].loc[(monthly_full[h].index.year >= BASELINE[0]) &
                                (monthly_full[h].index.year <= BASELINE[1])]
    ref_a = annual_full[h].loc[(annual_full[h].index.year >= BASELINE[0]) &
                              (annual_full[h].index.year <= BASELINE[1])]
    assert ref_m.complete.all() and len(ref_m) == 360
    assert ref_a.complete.all() and len(ref_a) == 30
    monthly_normals[h] = ref_m['mean'].groupby(ref_m.index.month).mean()
    annual_normals[h] = ref_a['mean'].mean()
    monthly[h] = aggregate_periods(frames[h], 'ME')
    annual[h] = aggregate_periods(frames[h], 'YE')
    monthly[h]['reference'] = pd.Series(monthly[h].index.month, index=monthly[h].index).map(monthly_normals[h])
    monthly[h]['anomaly'] = monthly[h]['mean'] - monthly[h]['reference']
    annual[h]['anomaly'] = annual[h]['mean'] - annual_normals[h]

ytd, ytd_series, ytd_normals = {}, {}, {}
for h, f in all_frames.items():
    all_ytd = matched_ytd(f, AS_OF, first_year=min(BASELINE[0], START_YEAR))
    ytd[h] = all_ytd.loc[START_YEAR:END_YEAR].reindex(YEARS).copy()
    ytd_series[h] = ytd[h]['mean']
    reference = all_ytd.loc[BASELINE[0]:BASELINE[1], 'mean']
    assert reference.notna().sum() == 30
    ytd_normals[h] = reference.mean()
    ytd[h]['anomaly'] = ytd[h]['mean'] - ytd_normals[h]
    keys = frames[h].index.strftime('%m-%d')
    keep = (keys <= AS_OF.strftime('%m-%d')) & (keys != '02-29')
    ytd[h]['provisional_days'] = frames[h].loc[keep, 'provisional'].groupby(frames[h].index[keep].year).sum().reindex(YEARS, fill_value=0)

parameters = dict(start_year=START_YEAR, end_year=END_YEAR, window_years=WINDOW_YEARS,
                  baseline=BASELINE, hac_lags=HAC_LAGS, alpha=ALPHA,
                  bootstrap_draws=BOOTSTRAP_DRAWS, seed=SEED,
                  period_coverage_required=1.0, matched_ytd_cutoff=AS_OF.strftime('%m-%d'),
                  include_provisional_primary=True, last_complete_year=LAST_COMPLETE_YEAR)
display(Markdown(f'**Primary window: {START_YEAR}–{END_YEAR}, inclusive ({len(YEARS)} calendar years, latest year included).**  \n'
                 f'**Latest observation:** {AS_OF:%d %B %Y}. **Execution (UTC):** {RUN_TIME.isoformat(timespec="seconds")}'))
display(pd.Series(parameters, name='declared setting').to_frame())

2. Window-specific quality and independent arithmetic check¶

Quality statistics here describe only the twenty-year analysis window. Source labels and input hashes identify the original data vintage. The daily global sum requires both hemispheres on the same day.

If the cached OSI SAF monthly validation snapshots from the full-record analysis match these exact input hashes, recomputed means are also checked against the provider's monthly text series only for these twenty years. Differences below 1 km² are consistent with text rounding; this validates aggregation arithmetic, not physical measurement accuracy. A missing or stale cache is explicitly skipped.

provenance, audits, source_rows = [], [], []
raw_hashes = {}
for h in ('nh', 'sh'):
    path = ROOT / f'osisaf_{h}_sie_daily.txt'
    header = [line for line in path.read_text().splitlines() if line.startswith('#')]
    expected_area = {'nh': 'Northern Hemisphere', 'sh': 'Southern Hemisphere'}[h]
    assert f'# Area: {expected_area}' in header
    assert any('Sea Ice Index v3.0' in line for line in header) and 'km^2' in header[0]
    raw_hashes[h] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    provenance.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'file': path.name, 'sha256': raw_hashes[h],
                        'creation_metadata': next(line for line in header if line.startswith('# Creation date:'))})
for h, f in frames.items():
    a, m = annual[h], monthly[h]
    assert len(a) == 20 and len(m) == 19 * 12 + AS_OF.month
    assert f.index.min() == pd.Timestamp(START_YEAR, 1, 1)
    assert f.index.max() == AS_OF
    assert len(ytd[h]) == 20 and ytd_series[h].notna().all()
    audits.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'calendar_days': len(f),
                   'missing_days': int(f.extent.isna().sum()),
                   'provider_interpolated_days': int(f.provider_interpolated.sum()),
                   'provider_extrapolated_days': int(f.provider_extrapolated.sum()),
                   'provisional_days': int(f.provisional.sum()),
                   'complete_months_including_provisional': int(m.complete.sum()),
                   'nominal_complete_months': int((m.complete & m.provisional_days.eq(0)).sum()),
                   'matched_ytd_years': int(ytd_series[h].notna().sum()),
                   'matched_days_per_year': int(ytd[h].expected_days.iloc[-1]),
                   'eligible_complete_years': int((a.complete & a.provisional_days.eq(0)).sum())})
    if h != 'global':
        for flag, group in f.groupby('source'):
            source_rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'flag': flag, 'days': len(group),
                                'first_date': group.index.min().date(), 'last_date': group.index.max().date()})
show_table('window_quality', pd.DataFrame(audits).set_index('region'))
show_table('source_flags', pd.DataFrame(source_rows))
show_table('input_provenance', pd.DataFrame(provenance).set_index('region'))

provider_validation = []
cache_dir = ROOT / 'artifacts' / 'sea_ice_monitoring'
cache_table = cache_dir / 'provider_monthly_validation.csv'
if cache_table.exists():
    cache = pd.read_csv(cache_table)
    matches = all(row.raw_daily_sha256 == raw_hashes[row.region] for row in cache.itertuples())
    if matches:
        for row in cache.itertuples():
            path = cache_dir / row.published_snapshot_file
            assert hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == row.published_snapshot_sha256
            p = pd.read_csv(path, comment='#', sep=r'\s+', names=['frac', 'year', 'month', 'day', 'extent'])
            p.index = pd.PeriodIndex.from_fields(year=p.year, month=p.month, freq='M')
            own = monthly[row.region]['mean'].copy() * 1e6
            own.index = own.index.to_period('M')
            pairs = pd.concat([own.rename('own'), p.extent.replace(-999, np.nan).rename('published')], axis=1).dropna()
            assert len(pairs) == int(monthly[row.region]['mean'].notna().sum())
            error = (pairs['own'] - pairs['published']).abs()
            assert error.max() < 1
            provider_validation.append({'region': NAMES[row.region], 'eligible_months': len(pairs),
                                         'max_abs_difference_km2': error.max(),
                                         'provider_snapshot_sha256': row.published_snapshot_sha256,
                                         'provider_url': row.published_url})
        show_table('provider_monthly_check', pd.DataFrame(provider_validation).set_index('region'), 6)
    else:
        display(Markdown('Cached provider validation belongs to different daily inputs; external check skipped.'))
else:
    display(Markdown('No cached provider monthly snapshots; external check skipped.'))

3. The headline twenty-year trajectory: matched YTD means¶

Every primary yearly point compares the same January 1–cutoff dates. For the current snapshot this is January 1–November 10, 314 days per year after omitting February 29. Consequently 2026 enters the fit as the twentieth observation, without comparing its partial-year mean against complete earlier years. The 2026 point is labelled and may contain provisional fast-track values.

Slopes describe this matched-season mean, not a full-calendar-year mean. The fitted change across the window multiplies the annual slope by the 19-year endpoint separation, although there are twenty yearly observations. Full-year supporting fits below use only genuinely complete nominal calendar years; 2026 remains missing there until complete and eligible.

ytd_fits, rows = {}, []
for h, s in ytd_series.items():
    fit = linear_trend(s, HAC_LAGS, ALPHA)
    ytd_fits[h] = fit
    rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'statistic': 'Matched Jan 1–cutoff mean, omitting Feb 29',
                  'cutoff': AS_OF.strftime('%m-%d'), 'days_per_year': int(ytd[h].expected_days.iloc[-1]),
                  **trend_record(fit), 'reference_ytd_mean': ytd_normals[h],
                  'percent_decade_of_reference': 100 * fit['slope_decade'] / ytd_normals[h],
                  'fitted_change_19_years': fit['slope_decade'] / 10 * (END_YEAR - START_YEAR),
                  'current_ytd_mean': s.loc[END_YEAR],
                  'current_ytd_provisional_days': int(ytd[h].loc[END_YEAR, 'provisional_days'])})
show_table('matched_ytd_trends', pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index('region'))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(12, 10), sharex=True, layout='constrained')
for ax, h in zip(axes, ('nh', 'sh', 'global')):
    s, fit = ytd_series[h], ytd_fits[h]
    ax.plot(s.index, s, 'o-', color=COLORS[h], lw=1.4, ms=4, label=f'Jan 1–{AS_OF:%b %d} matched mean')
    ax.scatter([END_YEAR], [s.loc[END_YEAR]], marker='D', s=65, color=COLORS[h], edgecolor='black',
               zorder=5, label=f'{END_YEAR}: includes available provisional values')
    ax.plot(YEARS, fit_values(fit, YEARS), color='#303030', lw=1.7, label='OLS, including latest year')
    ax.axhline(ytd_normals[h], color='0.4', ls=':', lw=1, label='1991–2020 matched reference')
    ax.set(title=f"{NAMES[h]} YTD: {fit['slope_decade']:+.3f} [{fit['ci_low']:+.3f}, {fit['ci_high']:+.3f}] per decade",
           ylabel=f'Matched YTD mean ({UNITS})')
    ax.legend(ncol=2, fontsize=8, loc='lower left')
axes[-1].set_xticks(sorted(set(np.arange(START_YEAR, END_YEAR + 1, 2)) | {END_YEAR}))
axes[-1].set_xlabel('Calendar year')
save_figure('01_twenty_year_ytd_trends', fig,
            f'{START_YEAR}–{END_YEAR}, same Jan 1–{AS_OF:%b %d} window in every year; no February 29. '
            'Intervals: conditional 95% HAC. Current year is included and may be revised.')

# Supporting full-calendar-year values never assign a full-year mean to partial 2026.
annual_series, annual_fits, rows = {}, {}, []
for h, a in annual.items():
    s = pd.Series(a['mean'].where(a.provisional_days.eq(0)).to_numpy(), index=a.index.year)
    annual_series[h] = s
    fit = linear_trend(s, HAC_LAGS, ALPHA)
    annual_fits[h] = fit
    rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'statistic': 'Supporting complete nominal calendar-year mean',
                  **trend_record(fit), 'reference_mean': annual_normals[h]})
show_table('annual_trends', pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index('region'))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(12, 9), sharex=True, layout='constrained')
for ax, h in zip(axes, ('nh', 'sh', 'global')):
    s, fit = annual_series[h], annual_fits[h]
    fit_years = np.arange(fit['first_year'], fit['last_year'] + 1)
    ax.plot(s.index, s, 'o-', color=COLORS[h], lw=1.2, ms=4, label='Complete nominal calendar-year mean')
    ax.plot(fit_years, fit_values(fit, fit_years), color='0.25', lw=1.5, label='Supporting fit, eligible years only')
    ax.axvspan(LAST_COMPLETE_YEAR + .5, END_YEAR + .4, color='0.9', label='No complete-year value yet')
    ax.set(title=f"{NAMES[h]}: n={fit['n']}, {fit['first_year']}–{fit['last_year']}", ylabel=f'Full-year mean ({UNITS})')
    ax.legend(ncol=2, fontsize=8, loc='lower left')
axes[-1].set_xlabel('Year')
save_figure('01b_supporting_complete_years', fig,
            'Supporting full-year series; the unfinished current year has no full-year value. '
            'Use matched YTD means above for the twenty-observation comparison including the latest year.')

4. Fixed-decade comparisons with equal coverage¶

The two groups are 2007–2016 and 2017–2026, ten years each. Their headline mean comparison uses the same matched YTD window in every year, including 2026. Seasonal monthly profiles compare only months with ten complete monthly means in each group: currently January–October. November and December are blank in this comparison, avoiding an unequal ten-versus-nine-year comparison. Counts and provisional-year flags are exported alongside each profile.

These are fixed, descriptive groups, not periods selected by searching for a break. The fixed 1991–2020 normal is a named historical reference, not an independent control sample. Differences are not causal or change-point tests.

decade_rows, seasonal_profiles = [], {}
for h, m in monthly.items():
    first, last = m.loc[m.index.year < MID_YEAR], m.loc[m.index.year >= MID_YEAR]
    early = first['mean'].groupby(first.index.month).agg(['mean', 'count']).reindex(range(1, 13))
    late = last['mean'].groupby(last.index.month).agg(['mean', 'count']).reindex(range(1, 13))
    comparable = early['count'].eq(10) & late['count'].eq(10)
    provisional = last.provisional_days.gt(0).groupby(last.index.month).sum().reindex(range(1, 13), fill_value=0)
    seasonal_profiles[h] = pd.DataFrame({
        'early_decade': early['mean'].where(comparable),
        'late_decade': late['mean'].where(comparable),
        'difference': (late['mean'] - early['mean']).where(comparable),
        'early_year_count': early['count'], 'late_year_count': late['count'],
        'equal_ten_year_coverage': comparable, 'late_provisional_years': provisional,
        'reference': monthly_normals[h]})
    s = ytd_series[h]
    decade_rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'statistic': 'Matched YTD mean', 'cutoff': AS_OF.strftime('%m-%d'),
                        'first_decade': f'{START_YEAR}–{MID_YEAR-1}', 'first_decade_mean': s.loc[START_YEAR:MID_YEAR-1].mean(),
                        'second_decade': f'{MID_YEAR}–{END_YEAR}', 'second_decade_mean': s.loc[MID_YEAR:END_YEAR].mean(),
                        'second_minus_first': s.loc[MID_YEAR:END_YEAR].mean() - s.loc[START_YEAR:MID_YEAR-1].mean()})
show_table('decade_mean_comparison', pd.DataFrame(decade_rows).set_index('region'))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 8), sharex=True, layout='constrained')
for j, h in enumerate(('nh', 'sh')):
    t = seasonal_profiles[h]
    axes[0, j].plot(t.index, t.early_decade, 'o-', color=COLORS[h], alpha=.55, lw=1.3, ms=3, label=f'{START_YEAR}–{MID_YEAR-1}')
    axes[0, j].plot(t.index, t.late_decade, 'o-', color=COLORS[h], lw=2, ms=3, label=f'{MID_YEAR}–{END_YEAR}')
    axes[0, j].plot(t.index, t.reference, '--', color='0.3', lw=1, label='1991–2020 mean')
    axes[0, j].set(title=NAMES[h], ylabel=f'Monthly extent ({UNITS})')
    axes[0, j].legend(fontsize=8)
    axes[1, j].bar(t.index, t.difference, color=COLORS[h], alpha=.85)
    for ax in axes[:, j]:
        for month in t.index[~t.equal_ten_year_coverage]:
            ax.axvspan(month - .45, month + .45, color='0.9', zorder=0)
    axes[1, j].axhline(0, color='0.3', lw=1)
    axes[1, j].set(ylabel=f'Second − first decade ({UNITS})', xlabel='Month')
    axes[1, j].set_xticks(range(1, 13), [calendar.month_abbr[k][0] for k in range(1, 13)])
save_figure('02_decade_seasonal_comparison', fig,
            'Monthly differences require ten complete means in each decade; grey = insufficient equal coverage. '
            'Recent complete months can contain provisional values. Headline decade means use matched YTD.')
for h, t in seasonal_profiles.items():
    show_table(f'decade_monthly_profile_{h}', t.rename_axis('month'))

5. Monthly anomalies within the twenty-year window¶

Monthly anomalies use the corresponding 1991–2020 calendar-month mean. The trailing twelve-month smoother requires twelve consecutive complete monthly observations. No earlier observation is included to initialize the smoother. The heatmaps use a common, symmetric colour scale and show all twenty calendar years including partial 2026. Grey cells denote incomplete or unavailable months. An asterisk identifies a completed month with provisional inputs.

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(12, 7), sharex=True, layout='constrained')
for ax, h in zip(axes, ('nh', 'sh')):
    m = monthly[h]
    ax.plot(m.index, m.anomaly, color=COLORS[h], alpha=.5, lw=1, label='Monthly anomaly')
    ax.plot(m.index, m.anomaly.rolling(12, min_periods=12).mean(), color=COLORS[h], lw=2, label='Trailing 12-month mean')
    provisional = m.loc[m.complete & m.provisional_days.gt(0)]
    ax.scatter(provisional.index, provisional.anomaly, facecolors='none', edgecolors='#B02B43', s=45, label='Provisional month')
    ax.axhline(0, color='0.3', lw=1)
    ax.axvline(pd.Timestamp('2025-01-01'), color='0.5', ls='--', lw=1)
    ax.set(title=NAMES[h], ylabel=f'Anomaly ({UNITS})')
    ax.legend(ncol=2, fontsize=8)
axes[-1].set_xlabel('Year')
save_figure('03_recent_monthly_anomalies', fig,
            'Fixed 1991–2020 reference; no data outside the declared twenty-year window enters these traces or smoothers.')

heatmaps = {}
for h, m in monthly.items():
    heatmaps[h] = m.assign(year=m.index.year, month=m.index.month).pivot(index='year', columns='month', values='anomaly').reindex(YEARS)
limit = max(np.nanmax(np.abs(heatmaps[h].to_numpy())) for h in ('nh', 'sh'))
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 7), sharey=True, layout='constrained')
cmap = mpl.colormaps['RdBu'].copy()
cmap.set_bad('#E5E5E5')
for ax, h in zip(axes, ('nh', 'sh')):
    im = ax.imshow(heatmaps[h], origin='lower', aspect='auto', cmap=cmap,
                   norm=TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-limit, vcenter=0, vmax=limit))
    for stamp in monthly[h].index[monthly[h].complete & monthly[h].provisional_days.gt(0)]:
        ax.text(stamp.month - 1, stamp.year - START_YEAR, '*', ha='center', va='center')
    ax.set_xticks(range(12), [calendar.month_abbr[k][0] for k in range(1, 13)])
    ax.set_yticks(range(20), YEARS)
    ax.set(title=NAMES[h], xlabel='Calendar month')
    ax.grid(False)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Year')
fig.colorbar(im, ax=axes, shrink=.8, label=f'Monthly anomaly ({UNITS})')
save_figure('04_recent_anomaly_heatmaps', fig,
            f'Only {START_YEAR}–{END_YEAR}. Red = below and blue = above the 1991–2020 monthly mean; same scale for both hemispheres. Grey = incomplete/unavailable; * = provisional inputs.')

6. Monthly trends including available 2026 months¶

Each month is fitted over all complete monthly values available in 2007–2026. Currently January–October have twenty observations; November and December have nineteen because those 2026 months are incomplete or unavailable. Every fit reports its actual sample size and endpoint year. Completed months containing provisional values participate in the primary estimate and are explicitly flagged. A nominal-only sensitivity check is included below.

Relative slopes divide by the same month's 1991–2020 mean. The 24 monthly fits are shown together with Holm-adjusted p-values. Bars are pointwise approximate 95% HAC intervals, not simultaneous or complete observational uncertainty bounds. Arctic September and Antarctic February remain predeclared indicators; both include their complete 2026 month in the current snapshot. statsmodels multiple-testing API.

monthly_series, monthly_fits, rows = {}, {}, []
for h in ('nh', 'sh'):
    m = monthly[h]
    for month in range(1, 13):
        subset = m.loc[m.index.month == month]
        s = pd.Series(subset['mean'].to_numpy(), index=subset.index.year).reindex(YEARS)
        result = linear_trend(s, HAC_LAGS, ALPHA)
        monthly_series[h, month], monthly_fits[h, month] = s, result
        ref = monthly_normals[h].loc[month]
        rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'month': month, 'month_name': calendar.month_abbr[month],
                      'reference_mean': ref, **trend_record(result),
                      'includes_latest_year': pd.notna(s.loc[END_YEAR]),
                      'provisional_years_in_fit': int((subset.complete & subset.provisional_days.gt(0)).sum()),
                      'percent_decade': 100 * result['slope_decade'] / ref,
                      'percent_low': 100 * result['ci_low'] / ref,
                      'percent_high': 100 * result['ci_high'] / ref})
monthly_trends = pd.DataFrame(rows)
monthly_trends['p_holm_24'] = multipletests(monthly_trends.pvalue, method='holm')[1]
show_table('monthly_trends', monthly_trends.set_index(['region', 'month_name']))
KEYS = [('nh', 9), ('sh', 2)]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 8), sharex=True, layout='constrained')
for j, h in enumerate(('nh', 'sh')):
    t = monthly_trends.loc[monthly_trends.region == NAMES[h]]
    for i, (value, low, high, label) in enumerate([
        ('slope_decade', 'ci_low', 'ci_high', f'{UNITS}/decade'),
        ('percent_decade', 'percent_low', 'percent_high', '% of reference / decade'),
    ]):
        ax = axes[i, j]
        ax.errorbar(t.month, t[value], yerr=np.vstack([t[value]-t[low], t[high]-t[value]]),
                    fmt='o-', color=COLORS[h], lw=1.3, capsize=3, ms=4)
        ax.axhline(0, color='0.3', lw=1)
        ax.set(title=NAMES[h] if i == 0 else '', ylabel=label)
        ax.set_xticks(range(1, 13), [calendar.month_abbr[k][0] for k in range(1, 13)])
save_figure('05_twenty_year_monthly_trends', fig,
            f'{START_YEAR}–{END_YEAR}. Pointwise 95% HAC intervals (3 year lags), n=20 for available 2026 months, otherwise n=19. Not simultaneous or measurement-error intervals.')

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5), layout='constrained')
key_rows = []
for ax, (h, month) in zip(axes, KEYS):
    s, fit = monthly_series[h, month], monthly_fits[h, month]
    ax.plot(s.index, s, 'o-', color=COLORS[h], ms=4, lw=1.2, label='Complete monthly mean')
    ax.plot(YEARS, fit_values(fit, YEARS), color='0.25', lw=1.7, label='Twenty-year linear fit')
    ax.set(title=f"{NAMES[h]} {calendar.month_name[month]}: {fit['slope_decade']:+.3f} per decade",
           xlabel='Year', ylabel=f'Extent ({UNITS})')
    ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc='lower left')
    ax.text(.03, .97, f"95% HAC CI [{fit['ci_low']:+.3f}, {fit['ci_high']:+.3f}]\nn={fit['n']}",
            transform=ax.transAxes, va='top', fontsize=9)
    key_rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'month': calendar.month_name[month], **trend_record(fit)})
save_figure('06_late_summer_recent_trends', fig,
            'A wide interval or one spanning zero is not proof of zero change. Fits describe the specified recent window only.')

7. Seasonal extrema in complete windows¶

Fixed windows reproduce the original notebook: Arctic minimum August–October, maximum February–April; Antarctic minimum January–March, maximum August–October. These are window-limited extrema, not automatically the calendar-year extrema. Every day in a window must exist. A centred 5-day-mean extreme tests sensitivity to daily noise; the complete five-day neighbourhood is required. Ties use the first date. No formal phenology trend is inferred from dates.

Every event year shown and fitted belongs to the twenty-year window, including completed 2026 windows. Incomplete event windows remain missing; available provisional inputs are included and their counts are retained. The shared extrema helper may internally enumerate earlier years, but they are discarded before any estimate, table, or plot is produced here.

extrema = {}
event_rows = []
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 8), sharex=True, layout='constrained')
for j, h in enumerate(('nh', 'sh')):
    # Include the neighbourhood outside the selected period for centred smoothing only.
    # Every selected event window is wholly within the analysis years.
    events = seasonal_extrema(all_frames[h], h, END_YEAR)
    extrema[h] = events.loc[events.year.between(START_YEAR, END_YEAR)].copy()
    for i, event in enumerate(('minimum', 'maximum')):
        t = extrema[h].loc[extrema[h].event == event].set_index('year')
        s = t.extent
        fit = linear_trend(s, HAC_LAGS, ALPHA)
        event_rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'event': event, 'window': t.window.iloc[0], **trend_record(fit)})
        ax = axes[i, j]
        ax.plot(t.index, t.extent, 'o-', color=COLORS[h], ms=3, lw=1.2, label='Daily extreme')
        ax.plot(t.index, t.smooth_extent, '--', color='0.25', lw=1, label='5-day-mean extreme')
        ax.set(title=f'{NAMES[h]} {event} · {t.window.iloc[0]}', ylabel=f'Extent ({UNITS})', xlabel='Year')
        ax.legend(fontsize=8)
save_figure('07_recent_seasonal_extrema', fig,
            'Complete seasonal windows only. Smoothing changes both the value and potentially the date of a daily extreme.')
show_table('seasonal_extrema_trends', pd.DataFrame(event_rows).set_index(['region', 'event']))

8. Short-record uncertainty and residual diagnostics¶

Twenty annual observations contain much less independent information than twenty years of daily rows might suggest. Daily measurements share seasonality, persistence, and retrieval assumptions; we do not inflate the sample size by fitting an independent-error daily trend.

Residual time traces and calendar-lag correlations are descriptive diagnostics. Persistent excursions or curvature warn that one linear mean plus stationary short-memory residuals may be inadequate. No independent-error confidence bars or automatic change-point selection are added to these diagnostics.

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 7), layout='constrained')
for j, (h, month) in enumerate(KEYS):
    r = monthly_fits[h, month]['residuals'].reindex(YEARS)
    ax = axes[0, j]
    ax.plot(r.index, r, 'o-', color=COLORS[h], ms=4, lw=1.2)
    ax.axhline(0, color='0.3', lw=1)
    ax.set(title=f'{NAMES[h]} {calendar.month_abbr[month]} residuals', xlabel='Year', ylabel=f'Residual ({UNITS})')
    correlations = []
    for lag in range(1, 6):
        pairs = pd.concat([r, r.shift(lag)], axis=1).dropna()
        correlations.append(pairs.iloc[:, 0].corr(pairs.iloc[:, 1]))
    axes[1, j].bar(range(1, 6), correlations, color=COLORS[h])
    axes[1, j].axhline(0, color='0.3', lw=1)
    axes[1, j].set(xlabel='Calendar-year lag', ylabel='Residual correlation', ylim=(-1, 1))
save_figure('08_recent_residual_diagnostics', fig,
            'Only 20 annual observations; residual correlations are noisy and descriptive. HAC does not repair model misspecification.')

Bandwidth, estimator, and residual-block bootstrap¶

HAC lags 0, 1, 3, and 5 vary the assumed dependence bandwidth; the OLS point estimate does not change. Theil–Sen provides a robust point estimate. A circular residual-block bootstrap uses 2-, 3-, and 5-year blocks, 4,000 replicates, fixed years, and a fixed seed. It requires contiguous annual observations. We report the 2.5th–97.5th percentiles of the bootstrap slopes.

These methods are sensitivity checks, not independent confirmations. The bootstrap assumes a linear mean and approximately stationary residuals; a five-year block in a twenty-year record leaves very limited effective replication. None propagates sensor/calibration uncertainty or demonstrates nominal interval coverage in this particular climate record.

band_rows, boot_rows, estimator_rows = [], [], []
for h, month in KEYS:
    s, primary = monthly_series[h, month], monthly_fits[h, month]
    estimator_rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'month': calendar.month_name[month],
                           'OLS_per_decade': primary['slope_decade'],
                           'Theil_Sen_per_decade': primary['theil_sen_decade']})
    for lag in (0, 1, 3, 5):
        band_rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'month': calendar.month_name[month], **trend_record(linear_trend(s, lag, ALPHA))})
    for block in (2, 3, 5):
        slopes = circular_block_bootstrap(s, block_length=block, draws=BOOTSTRAP_DRAWS, seed=SEED)
        lo, hi = np.quantile(slopes, [.025, .975])
        boot_rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'month': calendar.month_name[month], 'block_years': block,
                          'draws': BOOTSTRAP_DRAWS, 'seed': SEED,
                          'OLS_slope_decade': primary['slope_decade'], 'ci_low': lo, 'ci_high': hi,
                          'median_bootstrap_slope': np.median(slopes)})
bandwidth = pd.DataFrame(band_rows)
bootstrap = pd.DataFrame(boot_rows)
show_table('estimator_sensitivity', pd.DataFrame(estimator_rows).set_index('region'))
show_table('hac_bandwidth_sensitivity', bandwidth.set_index(['region', 'hac_lags']))
show_table('bootstrap_sensitivity', bootstrap.set_index(['region', 'block_years']))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5), layout='constrained')
for ax, (h, month) in zip(axes, KEYS):
    t = bandwidth.loc[bandwidth.region == NAMES[h]]
    b = bootstrap.loc[bootstrap.region == NAMES[h]]
    labels = [f'HAC {k}y' for k in t.hac_lags] + [f'Bootstrap block {k}y' for k in b.block_years]
    centers = np.r_[t.slope_decade, b.OLS_slope_decade]
    lo, hi = np.r_[t.ci_low, b.ci_low], np.r_[t.ci_high, b.ci_high]
    y = np.arange(len(labels))
    ax.hlines(y, lo, hi, color=COLORS[h], lw=2)
    ax.scatter(centers, y, s=25, color=COLORS[h])
    ax.set_yticks(y, labels)
    ax.axvline(0, color='0.3', lw=1)
    ax.invert_yaxis()
    ax.set(title=f'{NAMES[h]} {calendar.month_name[month]}', xlabel=f'Slope and 95% interval ({UNITS}/decade)')
save_figure('09_recent_uncertainty_sensitivity', fig,
            'HAC: approximate t intervals; bootstrap: residual-block percentile intervals. All points mark the same OLS estimate.')

9. Influence, fit-window, and observing-system sensitivity¶

Leave one year out: refit after removing each year in turn. This reveals influence, not a valid confidence interval and not a reason to discard an inconvenient observation. The covariance helper retains the omitted year as a calendar gap. Starting-year checks: move the start forward by two or four years, keeping the endpoint fixed. All fits remain inside the twenty-year window; overlapping fits cannot be read as independent tests of changing trends.

Sensor context: nominal AMSR2 enters the calibrated v3.0 record in January 2025, with a shorter September 2024 fill. Residual sensor differences remain possible. Ending at 2024 excludes the main 2025–2026 nominal input regime and changes both the endpoint and the instrument mix; that check cannot separate sensor bias from climate variability. We also mask provider-interpolated/extrapolated days and reapply strict monthly completeness, which may remove entire annual monthly observations. OSI SAF ATBD §§2.4.1, 4.1.2.

loo_rows, start_rows, observing_rows = [], [], []
for h, month in KEYS:
    s = monthly_series[h, month]
    for omitted in s.dropna().index:
        r = linear_trend(s.drop(omitted), HAC_LAGS, ALPHA)
        loo_rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'month': calendar.month_name[month],
                         'omitted_year': omitted, **trend_record(r)})
    for start in (START_YEAR, START_YEAR + 2, START_YEAR + 4):
        start_rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'month': calendar.month_name[month], 'declared_start': start,
                           **trend_record(linear_trend(s.loc[start:], HAC_LAGS, ALPHA))})
    early_end = min(2024, END_YEAR - 1)
    if early_end >= START_YEAR + 11:
        observing_rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'month': calendar.month_name[month],
                               'check': f'Endpoint {early_end} (pre-2025 when available)',
                               **trend_record(linear_trend(s.loc[:early_end], HAC_LAGS, ALPHA))})
    alternative = frames[h].copy()
    alternative.loc[alternative.provider_interpolated | alternative.provider_extrapolated, 'extent'] = np.nan
    m = aggregate_periods(alternative, 'ME')
    m = m.loc[m.index.month == month]
    filtered = pd.Series(m['mean'].to_numpy(), index=m.index.year).reindex(YEARS)
    observing_rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'month': calendar.month_name[month],
                           'check': 'Mask provider-filled days; require complete month',
                           **trend_record(linear_trend(filtered, HAC_LAGS, ALPHA))})
    nominal_monthly = monthly[h].loc[monthly[h].index.month == month]
    nominal_series = pd.Series(nominal_monthly['mean'].where(nominal_monthly.provisional_days.eq(0)).to_numpy(),
                               index=nominal_monthly.index.year).reindex(YEARS)
    observing_rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'month': calendar.month_name[month],
                           'check': 'Nominal-only completed months',
                           **trend_record(linear_trend(nominal_series, HAC_LAGS, ALPHA))})

# Recompare every year's YTD window at the common last nominal observation date.
nominal_cutoff = min(f.loc[f.extent.notna() & ~f.provisional & (f.index <= AS_OF)].index[-1]
                     for f in all_frames.values())
nominal_ytd_rows = []
for h, f in all_frames.items():
    nominal_ytd = matched_ytd(f, nominal_cutoff, first_year=START_YEAR).loc[START_YEAR:END_YEAR, 'mean']
    # Require the actual compared window to contain no provisional observations.
    keys = frames[h].index.strftime('%m-%d')
    subset = frames[h].loc[(keys <= nominal_cutoff.strftime('%m-%d')) & (keys != '02-29')]
    assert not subset.provisional.any()
    nominal_ytd_rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'shared_cutoff': nominal_cutoff.strftime('%m-%d'),
                             **trend_record(linear_trend(nominal_ytd, HAC_LAGS, ALPHA))})
show_table('nominal_only_matched_ytd', pd.DataFrame(nominal_ytd_rows).set_index('region'))
loo, start_checks = pd.DataFrame(loo_rows), pd.DataFrame(start_rows)
show_table('leave_one_year_out', loo.set_index(['region', 'omitted_year']))
show_table('start_year_sensitivity', start_checks.set_index(['region', 'declared_start']))
show_table('observing_system_sensitivity', pd.DataFrame(observing_rows).set_index(['region', 'check']))

10. Global matched-YTD extent and hemispheric contributions¶

Global extent is the same-date Arctic plus Antarctic sum. Its matched-YTD slope equals the sum of hemispheric matched-YTD slopes when all three use the same eligible years and daily weights, including 2026. Confidence limits do not add; the global fit captures covariance between hemispheric fluctuations.

The upper plot uses the same January 1–cutoff window in every year; the lower plot uses completed monthly anomalies within the declared window. Recent complete months can still be provisional. The global sum measures extent, not ice volume or a causal contribution to energy balance.

assert all(ytd_series[h].notna().all() for h in frames)
np.testing.assert_allclose(ytd_series['global'], ytd_series['nh'] + ytd_series['sh'], atol=1e-12)
np.testing.assert_allclose(ytd_fits['global']['slope_decade'],
                           ytd_fits['nh']['slope_decade'] + ytd_fits['sh']['slope_decade'], atol=1e-12)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(12, 7), sharex=True, layout='constrained')
for h in ('nh', 'sh', 'global'):
    a = ytd[h]
    stamps = pd.to_datetime(a.index.astype(str) + '-07-01')
    axes[0].plot(stamps, a.anomaly, 'o-', color=COLORS[h], ms=3,
                 lw=2 if h == 'global' else 1.2, label=NAMES[h])
    m = monthly[h]
    axes[1].plot(m.index, m.anomaly.rolling(12, min_periods=12).mean(),
                 color=COLORS[h], lw=2 if h == 'global' else 1.2, label=NAMES[h])
axes[0].set(title='Matched-YTD anomalies, including the latest year', ylabel=f'Matched YTD anomaly ({UNITS})')
axes[0].legend(ncol=3)

11. Generated findings for this twenty-year window¶

The following statements are computed from the declared period. Read them with the dependence diagnostics, influence checks, sensor caveats, and conditional nature of the reported intervals. A rate over these twenty years is not a claim about the longer record or the next twenty years.

findings = [f'# Sea-ice extent, {START_YEAR}–{END_YEAR} through {AS_OF:%d %B %Y}', '',
            f'Twenty calendar years including partial {END_YEAR}; reference {BASELINE[0]}–{BASELINE[1]}; units million km².', '',
            f'## Primary matched YTD: Jan 1–{AS_OF:%B %d}, excluding February 29', '']
for h in ('nh', 'sh', 'global'):
    r = ytd_fits[h]
    findings.append(f"- **{NAMES[h]}:** {r['slope_decade']:+.3f} million km² per decade; conditional 95% HAC interval "
                    f"[{r['ci_low']:+.3f}, {r['ci_high']:+.3f}], n={r['n']}, including {END_YEAR}. "
                    f"Current YTD mean {ytd_series[h].loc[END_YEAR]:.3f}; "
                    f"{int(ytd[h].loc[END_YEAR, 'provisional_days'])} provisional days in that current-year window.")
findings += ['', '## Late-summer monthly means including 2026', '']
for h, month in KEYS:
    r = monthly_fits[h, month]
    crosses = r['ci_low'] <= 0 <= r['ci_high']
    interpretation = ('The interval spans zero; this does not establish stability or recovery.' if crosses else
                      'The interval excludes zero conditional on the stated model; it excludes full observational/model uncertainty.')
    findings.append(f"- **{NAMES[h]} {calendar.month_name[month]}:** {r['slope_decade']:+.3f} million km² per decade "
                    f"[{r['ci_low']:+.3f}, {r['ci_high']:+.3f}], n={r['n']}, last included year {r['last_year']}. {interpretation}")
findings += ['', '## Fixed-decade matched-YTD comparison', '']
for row in tables['decade_mean_comparison'].reset_index().itertuples():
    findings.append(f'- **{row.region}:** matched YTD mean in {MID_YEAR}–{END_YEAR} is '
                    f'{row.second_minus_first:+.3f} million km² relative to {START_YEAR}–{MID_YEAR-1} (descriptive difference).')
findings += ['', '## Scope and interpretation', '',
    f'- The twenty-year window is {START_YEAR}–{END_YEAR}; {START_YEAR-1} is excluded. {END_YEAR} enters primary matched-YTD fits and each completed available month or event window.',
    f'- No full-calendar-year mean is assigned to unfinished {END_YEAR}. Supporting full-year fits use eligible years only and report n separately.',
    '- Completed monthly trends use their actual observation counts; unfinished months stay missing. Equal-decade seasonal differences require ten complete values in each group.',
    '- Recent fast-track estimates are provisional and can change. A nominal-only YTD sensitivity reuses an earlier cutoff in all twenty years.',
    '- All statistical intervals are conditional on the chosen model and do not propagate full measurement/calibration uncertainty. No acceleration, structural break, or future trajectory is inferred.']
findings_text = '\n'.join(findings)
display(Markdown(findings_text))

Primary matched YTD: Jan 1–November 10, excluding February 29¶

  • Arctic: -0.226 million km² per decade; conditional 95% HAC interval [-0.370, -0.082], n=20, including 2026. Current YTD mean 10.447; 15 provisional days in that current-year window.
  • Antarctic: -0.916 million km² per decade; conditional 95% HAC interval [-1.315, -0.516], n=20, including 2026. Current YTD mean 11.033; 15 provisional days in that current-year window.
  • Global sum: -1.142 million km² per decade; conditional 95% HAC interval [-1.523, -0.761], n=20, including 2026. Current YTD mean 21.480; 15 provisional days in that current-year window.

Late-summer monthly means including 2026¶

  • Arctic September: +0.020 million km² per decade [-0.183, +0.223], n=20, last included year 2026. The interval spans zero; this does not establish stability or recovery.
  • Antarctic February: -0.620 million km² per decade [-0.952, -0.288], n=20, last included year 2026. The interval excludes zero conditional on the stated model; it excludes full observational/model uncertainty.

Fixed-decade matched-YTD comparison¶

  • Arctic: matched YTD mean in 2017–2026 is -0.265 million km² relative to 2007–2016 (descriptive difference).
  • Antarctic: matched YTD mean in 2017–2026 is -1.190 million km² relative to 2007–2016 (descriptive difference).
  • Global sum: matched YTD mean in 2017–2026 is -1.455 million km² relative to 2007–2016 (descriptive difference).

Scope and interpretation¶

  • The twenty-year window is 2007–2026; 2006 is excluded. 2026 enters primary matched-YTD fits and each completed available month or event window.
  • No full-calendar-year mean is assigned to unfinished 2026. Supporting full-year fits use eligible years only and report n separately.
  • Completed monthly trends use their actual observation counts; unfinished months stay missing. Equal-decade seasonal differences require ten complete values in each group.
  • Recent fast-track estimates are provisional and can change. A nominal-only YTD sensitivity reuses an earlier cutoff in all twenty years.
  • All statistical intervals are conditional on the chosen model and do not propagate full measurement/calibration uncertainty. No acceleration, structural break, or future trajectory is inferred.

12. Latest 2026 conditions within the twenty-year window¶

The latest day and matched YTD mean are ranked against 2007–2026, including the current year once: twenty years, rather than twenty historical years plus an extra current year. Ties use minimum rank; rank 1 means lowest extent. These are ordinal descriptions, not significance tests or return periods.

The daily seasonal plot shows 2026 through the actual observation date, with provisional values dashed, alongside the 2007–2025 same-date interannual spread. Recent fast-track data use AMSR3 from September 2026 while nominal input remains AMSR2; they may be revised. OSI SAF service announcement.

latest_rows = []
for h, f in all_frames.items():
    observed = with_anomalies(f, climatologies[h])
    row = observed.loc[AS_OF]
    same_day = observed.loc[(observed.index.strftime('%m-%d') == AS_OF.strftime('%m-%d')) &
                           in_window(observed.index) & (observed.index <= AS_OF), 'extent'].dropna()
    pool = ytd_series[h].dropna()
    value = pool.loc[END_YEAR]
    latest_rows.append({'region': NAMES[h], 'date': AS_OF.date(), 'current_extent': row.extent,
                        'anomaly_vs_1991_2020': row.anomaly,
                        'same_day_low_rank': int((same_day < row.extent).sum() + 1),
                        'same_day_comparison_years': len(same_day),
                        'provisional_latest_day': bool(row.provisional), 'matched_ytd_mean': value,
                        'ytd_low_rank': int((pool < value).sum() + 1), 'ytd_comparison_years': len(pool)})
show_table('latest_state', pd.DataFrame(latest_rows).set_index('region'))

13. Export and reproducibility checks¶

All primary period tables and daily anomaly exports below are restricted to the twenty-year window. The manifest identifies the older reference period separately, records input/module/notebook-source hashes, packages, and settings, and names the figure bundle. Source attribution is EUMETSAT OSI SAF, Sea-Ice Index (2026), OSI-420-a, doi:10.15770/EUM_SAF_OSI_0026, CC BY 4.0. Detailed methodological sources are in docs/sea_ice_methods_sources.md.

To update, refresh the raw files with python update_data.py, then restart and run this notebook. The twenty-year window ends in the year of the latest observation, including its available partial record; the matched YTD cutoff advances with that record. Exports overwrite this directory, so archive it first if retaining dated releases. Shared-method tests run with python -m unittest discover -s tests -v.

assert len(YEARS) == 20 and END_YEAR - START_YEAR == 19
for h in frames:
    assert frames[h].index.year.min() == START_YEAR and frames[h].index.year.max() == END_YEAR
    assert frames[h].index.max() == AS_OF
    assert len(ytd_series[h]) == 20 and ytd_series[h].notna().all()
    assert ytd_fits[h]['n'] == 20 and ytd_fits[h]['last_year'] == END_YEAR
    assert ytd[h].valid_days.eq(ytd[h].expected_days).all()
    assert ytd[h].expected_days.nunique() == 1
    assert (monthly[h].loc[~monthly[h].complete, 'mean'].isna()).all()
    if AS_OF < pd.Timestamp(END_YEAR, 12, 31):
        assert pd.isna(annual_series[h].loc[END_YEAR]), 'Partial current year cannot have a full-year mean.'
    daily[h].to_csv(OUTPUT / f'daily_{h}.csv', index_label='date')
    monthly[h].to_csv(OUTPUT / f'monthly_{h}.csv', index_label='date')
    annual[h].to_csv(OUTPUT / f'annual_{h}.csv', index_label='date')
    ytd[h].to_csv(OUTPUT / f'matched_ytd_{h}.csv', index_label='year')
for key, result in monthly_fits.items():
    assert result['first_year'] >= START_YEAR and result['last_year'] <= END_YEAR
    assert len(monthly_series[key]) == 20
    assert result['n'] == monthly_series[key].notna().sum()
for h, t in extrema.items():
    assert t.year.between(START_YEAR, END_YEAR).all()
    t.to_csv(OUTPUT / f'seasonal_events_{h}.csv', index=False)
for name, table in tables.items():
    table.to_csv(OUTPUT / f'{name}.csv')
